HUNTING STUDIES, 2026-10-08
Three ways to act on a big move, measured on 45 sessions of the whole US market. Costs taken off. Doing nothing scores 0%.

1. FLAG STUDY
A jump of 20%+ on at least 5x normal volume, then 3+ quiet days on drying volume, then a break above the quiet range. Bought on the break, stop at the bottom of the range, out after 5 sessions.

CONCLUSION: Too few finished flag trades in these 45 sessions to judge. It needs more weeks.

What became of 301 heavy-volume jumps: 262 never formed a flag, 17 formed one and broke down, 8 went nowhere, 2 gapped away with no fair entry, 12 broke out and gave an entry.
All flag trades: average -3.7%, typical -2.1%, 33% ended higher (12 trades)
5 USD and over: average -2.2%, typical -3.5%, 33% ended higher (9 trades)
Under 5 USD: average -8.2%, typical -2.1%, 33% ended higher (3 trades)
Compare, buying the morning after the jump: typical -4.5%, 38% ended higher (836 cases).

2. FLAG PULLBACK (after the break, wait for a return to the break level that holds)
5 USD and over: average +19.3%, typical +3.1%, 67% ended higher (3 trades)

3. EXPANSION DAY (up 1.5x its normal daily range or more on 2x volume or more; bought at the next open; stop 1x that range, target 3x, out after 10 sessions)
5 USD and over: average -1.2%, typical -2.3%, 23% ended higher (470 trades). Of these, 14% reached the target, 75% hit the stop, 11% ran out of time.
Under 5 USD: average -1.5%, typical -5.4%, 17% ended higher (88 trades)
CONCLUSION: the expansion day did NOT make money in this sample. Do not trade it.
A target three times the stop is reached far less often than the stop. The numbers above are what that trade-off really paid.
